title: tenant-shaper-and-graceful-decommissioning-for-dedicated-pools
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated pools asked for smoother capacity rebalancing when tenants change committed throughput and for a safe, observable path to drain nodes out of a fleet without disrupting tenant SLAs. This PR introduces a tenant-level shaping layer that (1) smooths abrupt throughput reductions, (2) packs tenants more efficiently across GPUs, and (3) adds a graceful decommissioning protocol (drain-probe + staged eviction) that maintains per-tenant throughput guarantees during node drain.

Design summary: The tenant shaper sits in the request router and enforces a short horizon rate profile per tenant derived from committed throughput, observed burst allowance, and recent token usage. It exposes a per-tenant 'shape window' that controls the steady-state token dispatch rate and a temporary 'elastic headroom' that can be borrowed/repaid. When a node is scheduled for decommission, a drain-probe step probes actual tail-latency and queue-utilization; if safe, the controller triggers staged cross-tenant placement moves with a backoff so SLOs degrade minimally.

What changed (high-level):
- Add router/tenant_shaper service with smoothing algorithm, borrowing accounting, and eviction hints.
- Controller flow: drain-probe -> placement plan -> staged-migrate + replicate-fallback.
- Scheduler updates: new allocation scorer that prefers packing affinity but respects tenant throughput SLOs.
- New Prometheus metrics and tracing spans for shaping decisions, probe outcomes, and migration progress.
- E2E and unit tests for borrowing/repayment, drain-probe gating, and metric rollup.

Compatibility and rollout: The default shaper is OFF for existing customers. A feature flag per-tenant enables it; rollout will start with internal Dedicated fleets and then opt-in customers. The drain protocol is backward-compatible: nodes without the controller will still be drainable via existing decommission paths.

Telemetry and alerting: Introduces tenant_shaper_effective_rate, tenant_shaper_borrowed_tokens, drain_probe_success, staged_migration_progress. Alerts suggested in release_notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation and unit tests
- [x] Integration tests with small dedicated cluster harness
- [x] Observability: metrics + tracing
- [x] rollout feature flag + migration plan
- [x] Docs PR (separate) linked

Related: ENG-4821 implements the shaping algorithm; SUP-1219 is the customer support case that motivated staged migration.

Notes on behaviour and limits: Borrowed headroom is bounded to a tenant-configured percentage of committed throughput and is repaid within a configured window (default 10m). The shaping window defaults to 30s smoothing with exponential backoff for rapid spikes. The staged-migrate plan attempts to move one tenant at a time per affected node to avoid cascading bursts.

Testing notes: Ran the bench-harness with 3 workloads: interactive chat (low qps, bursty), embedding batch (steady high throughput), and mixed multi-tenant load. Observed 12-18% better packing efficiency vs baseline with no increase in 99th percentile latency during drains when shaper is enabled and tuned.

release_notes: Added tenant-level shaping for smoother capacity changes, a graceful drain protocol (drain-probe + staged migration), new metrics for shaping and decommissioning, and a per-tenant feature flag to opt in. Recommended alerts: tenant_shaper_borrowed_tokens > 0 for >15m (investigate misconfig), drain_probe_failure rate > 5% over 10m.
discussion: Rafael Ortiz: Overall this looks good — two requested changes: make the default borrow window configurable via CLI and add an integration smoke in the canary job.

Priya Kapoor: The staged-migration backoff constants look conservative; can we make them adaptive based on current cluster utilization?
Maya Chen: Good point. I added a simple utilization multiplier (scheduler will multiply base backoff by 1 + util*0.5). We can iterate on this metric in a follow-up if needed.
